learning_goal: Date implantation day by day from apposition to full burial, name the two trophoblast layers and say which one invades, explain how the lacunae become the first uteroplacental circulation, and predict what goes wrong when the site or the depth is abnormal.

structures.name: Uterine surface epithelium
structures.label: Uterine surface epithelium
structures.narration: The endometrium is not receptive for most of the cycle. Progesterone from the corpus luteum opens a short window in the mid-secretory phase, roughly cycle days twenty to twenty-four, when the surface throws up pinopodes and expresses the adhesion molecules the blastocyst needs. Outside that window the same blastocyst will not stick. Two clocks must agree — the embryo must arrive hatched and ready at exactly the days the wall is willing.
structures.narration_from: sequence-version structure "receptive_window" — carried across verbatim. In the SVG scene that was a teaching BEAT about a STATE of the wall, with no geometry; here the thing the state is a state OF — the luminal epithelium — is a built structure, and the beat that narrates the window is view 1. The words are unchanged. What the model does NOT draw is pinopodes or an adhesion molecule: at 10 um per unit a pinopode is a tenth of a unit, and drawing one would be an invention. Declared in gaps[].

structures.name: Decidua basalis — deep to the conceptus
structures.label: Decidua basalis — deep to the conceptus
structures.narration: The mother is not passive. Stromal cells around the implantation site swell with glycogen and lipid and become decidual cells. They feed the embryo before there is any circulation, and they also fence it in — a decidua that forms properly is what stops the trophoblast digging deeper than it should. Where that barrier fails you get an abnormally adherent placenta.
structures.narration_from: sequence-version structure "decidua" — carried across verbatim, WHOLE, on the basalis. Every clause of it is true of this third of the tissue: it is the part that swells deep to the embryo, the part that feeds it before any circulation exists, the part whose failure lets the placenta dig into muscle, and the part that becomes the maternal side of the placenta. It is placed here rather than duplicated across all three because blastocyst.js's round-4 review found that a narration marked "verbatim" on both halves of a split structure can be FALSE of one of them, and "it also fences it in" is a statement about the decidua UNDER the trophoblast.

structures.name: Decidua parietalis — the rest of the wall
structures.label: Decidua parietalis — the rest of the wall
structures.narration: Three names for the same tissue in three positions. Basalis lies deep to the embryo and becomes the maternal side of the placenta. Capsularis is the thin layer stretched over it towards the uterine cavity. Parietalis lines the rest of the uterus. As the sac grows, capsularis and parietalis meet and fuse and the uterine cavity is obliterated by about week twelve.
structures.narration_from: sequence-version structure "decidua_parts" — carried across verbatim, WHOLE, and DELIBERATELY ON BOTH of capsularis and parietalis. Nothing is altered and nothing is dropped.

structures.name: Uterine gland
structures.label: Uterine gland
structures.narration: One secretory gland, opening on the surface. It is here as the thing that says this is a secretory endometrium under progesterone and not any other epithelial surface — the glands are coiled and actively secreting in the implantation window, and their secretion is what the blastocyst lives on for the few days between hatching and a circulation.
structures.narration_from: WRITTEN 2026-10-03 by the model3d build run. A 3D wall has to look like one, and a reader who cannot tell proliferative from secretory endometrium cannot date the picture.

structures.name: Maternal spiral artery
structures.label: Maternal spiral artery
structures.narration: A maternal spiral artery, coiling up through the stroma towards the site. It is drawn from day six because it is there from day six: what changes in week two is not that the mother has vessels but that the syncytiotrophoblast opens one.
structures.narration_from: WRITTEN 2026-10-03 by the model3d build run. Not SVG-era text: the SVG scene narrated "the syncytiotrophoblast has eroded the walls of maternal capillaries" with nothing drawn to be eroded. A beat cannot show a vessel opening into a lacuna unless the vessel is in the picture before it opens.

structures.name: Maternal blood
structures.label: Maternal blood
structures.narration: By day eleven or twelve the syncytiotrophoblast has eroded the walls of maternal capillaries and their blood spills into the lacunae. That is the start of the uteroplacental circulation. Note what it means: maternal blood now bathes fetal tissue directly, with no vessel wall between them. The human placenta is haemochorial for the rest of the pregnancy because of what happens in these two days.
structures.narration_from: sequence-version structure "sinusoids" — carried across verbatim. The ref is UNPINNED, and that is the honest reading of this structure rather than a convenience: maternal blood is in the wall from day six, and what day eleven changes is not whether there is blood but where it can go. So the part exists at every t — in the artery early, in the lacunae late — which is also what makes it safe against engine__procedural-ref-default-t. See the model's header, section 3.

structures.name: The original luminal surface
structures.label: The original luminal surface
structures.narration: The level the uterine surface was at before anything happened, kept in the picture as a collar round the rim of the patch. Everything this topic is examined on is a statement about this line: the embryo starts above it, ends below it, and the surface closes over the top.
structures.narration_from: WRITTEN 2026-10-03 by the model3d build run. Not SVG-era text: a reference, not a tissue. structures.name: Trophoblast — one layer, not yet two
structures.label: Trophoblast — one layer, not yet two
structures.narration: Before contact there is one trophoblast, not two. The wall of the hatched blastocyst is a single layer, and it is adhesion that makes it split — which is why the order apposition, adhesion, invasion is asked as an order. The two layers beat 5 names do not exist yet in this picture.

structures.name: Syncytiotrophoblast — the outer layer
structures.label: Syncytiotrophoblast — the outer layer
structures.narration: The outer layer, and the aggressive one. Its cells have fused into a single multinucleate mass with no borders between nuclei, which is exactly what a tissue built to burrow needs — no gaps for the mother's cells to get through. It does three jobs: it invades, it forms the lacunae, and it makes hCG. If a question asks which layer invades or which layer secretes, the answer to both is this one.
structures.narration_from: sequence-version structure "syncytiotrophoblast" — carried across verbatim. Drawn at 0.52 opacity in every beat that shows the lacunae, because the lacunae ARE the spaces inside it and an opaque shell hides the beat's whole subject. RENDER-STANDARD 3.x is explicit that this is what a teaching figure does. The containment is published in the model's PARTITION rather than tolerated.

structures.name: Cytotrophoblast — the inner layer
structures.label: Cytotrophoblast — the inner layer
structures.narration: The inner layer, sitting against the embryo. Its cells are single-nucleus, have clear borders, and keep dividing — this is the layer that supplies new cells. It does not invade. Think of it as the factory: every syncytiotrophoblast nucleus was once a cytotrophoblast cell that divided and then fused outward.
structures.narration_from: sequence-version structure "cytotrophoblast" — carried across verbatim.

structures.name: Blastocyst cavity
structures.label: Blastocyst cavity
structures.narration: The cavity the blastocyst arrived with. It is still here through the whole of week two, and it becomes the chorionic cavity — so the space a student meets as "the blastocyst cavity" on day five and as "the extraembryonic coelom" in week three is one continuous space that was never refilled.
structures.narration_from: WRITTEN 2026-10-03 by the model3d build run. Not SVG-era text: the SVG scene began at apposition and had no structure for the cavity. It is in this model because the cut beats would otherwise show a solid ball, and because the continuity with blastocyst.js's own blastocoele is worth a sentence.

structures.name: Embryoblast — the bilaminar disc
structures.label: Embryoblast — the bilaminar disc
structures.narration: The inner cell mass, flattening as week two goes on into the bilaminar disc of epiblast and hypoblast. The embryo proper is the smallest thing in this picture and everything else here exists to supply it.
structures.narration_from: WRITTEN 2026-10-03 by the model3d build run. structures.name: Embryonic pole
structures.label: Embryonic pole
structures.narration: The pole the inner cell mass sits at. It is the pole that apposes first, the pole the trophoblast thickens over, and the pole that invades — three facts with one answer, which is why it is worth marking rather than describing.
structures.narration_from: WRITTEN 2026-10-03 by the model3d build run. Not SVG-era text: a marker. The model's section 8 records the version that was a spike and why acceptance row M rejected it.

structures.name: Trophoblastic lacunae — the lacunar stage
structures.label: Trophoblastic lacunae — the lacunar stage
structures.narration: Around day eight vacuoles appear inside the syncytiotrophoblast and run together into larger spaces called lacunae. They are holes in a tissue, not vessels — nothing lines them. But they are the beginning of the intervillous space of the placenta, so the adult organ starts as gaps in an invading cell mass.
structures.narration_from: sequence-version structure "lacunae" — carried across verbatim. The later, confluent, blood-filled lacunae are a second key, as cardiac-looping's stages are.

structures.label: Primary villi

views.title: Invasion — day 7 to 9

ops.kind: digests it, and sinks into the space it makes

views.narration:
Step three is digestion. The syncytiotrophoblast releases proteolytic enzymes, breaks through the surface epithelium and eats its way into the stroma, and the whole embryo sinks below the surface. In the human this is interstitial implantation — the embryo ends up buried inside the wall, not sitting on it, and that is a species difference examiners like.

Three steps over about three days. Day six, the blastocyst lies against the endometrium embryonic pole first — apposition, still loose. Day six to seven, integrins lock it on — adhesion, and now it cannot be washed away. Day seven to nine, the syncytiotrophoblast digests its way through the surface epithelium and the embryo sinks into the stroma — invasion. In humans the embryo ends up buried inside the wall, which is called interstitial implantation.

views.title: One trophoblast becomes two

views.narration: At contact the trophoblast splits into two layers and you must be able to tell them apart. The inner cytotrophoblast has single nuclei and visible cell borders and keeps dividing; it is the source of new cells and it does not invade. The outer syncytiotrophoblast is one fused multinucleate mass with no borders; it invades, it forms the lacunae, and it makes the hormones. Cells move one way only — cytotrophoblast divides and fuses outward into the syncytium.

deferred_beats.title: The pregnancy announces itself
deferred_beats.narration:
The syncytiotrophoblast secretes hCG as soon as it starts invading. hCG acts on the LH receptor of the corpus luteum, progesterone keeps flowing, and the endometrium is not shed — so the first sign of implantation is a period that does not come. Blood levels are detectable about eight days after fertilization. Remember what a pregnancy test is measuring: a product of the future placenta, not of the embryo. By week eight the placenta itself makes the progesterone and the corpus luteum is no longer needed.

From the moment it invades, the syncytiotrophoblast secretes hCG. It acts on the corpus luteum's LH receptor and keeps progesterone flowing, so the endometrium is not shed and the period is missed. It is detectable in blood about eight days after fertilization, which is why a test can be positive before a period is late. The placenta takes over progesterone production at about week eight and the corpus luteum is then dispensable.
deferred_beats.why_not_a_view: NOTHING IN IT CAN BE DRAWN AT THIS SCALE. The beat is about hCG acting on the corpus luteum, and the corpus luteum is in the ovary — centimetres away from a 2.6 mm patch of uterine wall drawn at 10 um per unit. Putting it in the frame would need a scale break of about three orders of magnitude, and RENDER-STANDARD is explicit that a model may not fake what it cannot draw. The hormone itself has no form at all. A beat that highlighted the syncytiotrophoblast and talked about hCG would be the same frame as beat 5 with different words, which RENDER-STANDARD calls text; text has its own home in this app.
deferred_beats.where_it_belongs: the sequence and diagram modes, both of which are in deferred_modes — a panel can draw an ovary beside a uterus and an arrow between them, which is exactly the thing a true-scale 3D model cannot. The clinically essential half (a pregnancy test measures a product of the future placenta, and a missed period is the first sign of implantation) is pure physiology and belongs in prose.

deferred_beats.title: Wrong place, wrong depth
deferred_beats.narration:
Everything clinical here follows from one fact: the trophoblast invades whatever it lands on. Land in the ampulla of the tube and you get an ectopic pregnancy in a thin wall that ruptures and bleeds into the abdomen. Land low in the uterus and the placenta covers the internal os as a praevia. Land on a caesarean scar with no decidua to stop it and the placenta grows into the muscle — accreta, increta, percreta — and will not separate at delivery. And if invasion is too shallow to remodel the spiral arteries, the placenta is underperfused for the whole pregnancy, which is where pre-eclampsia and much growth restriction begin. Two weeks of embryology explains half of third-trimester obstetrics.

The trophoblast will implant into almost any surface it meets, which is the whole danger. Most ectopics are in the ampulla of the uterine tube, where the wall is thin and rupture with severe intraperitoneal bleeding is the emergency. Anything that slows tubal transport — previous pelvic infection, tubal surgery — raises the risk. At the other end, a blastocyst that implants low in the uterus places the placenta over or near the internal os, and that is a placenta praevia presenting later as painless bright red bleeding.

Invasion has to be deep enough and no deeper. Too deep, usually where a caesarean scar has left no decidua to stop it, and the placenta grows into the myometrium — accreta into it, increta through the muscle, percreta out beyond the serosa — so it will not separate at delivery and the haemorrhage can cost the uterus. Too shallow, and the trophoblast fails to remodel the maternal spiral arteries into wide low-resistance channels; the placenta stays underperfused, and that is the accepted origin of pre-eclampsia and much fetal growth restriction. Both diseases are settled in these fourteen days.
deferred_beats.why_not_a_view: IT NEEDS FOUR THINGS THIS MODEL DOES NOT CONTAIN. An ectopic needs the ampulla of the uterine tube; a praevia needs the internal os; accreta, increta and percreta need the MYOMETRIUM, and this model draws a window on the superficial 2 mm of a 5-7 mm endometrium with no myometrium in it at all (see the model's ACCEPTANCE.scale); and the shallow-invasion end of it needs remodelled spiral arteries over weeks, not days. Each of those is a scale break or an invention, and the four together are a different scene rather than a beat of this one. The honest thing a 3D model can say here is what beat 10 already shows and measures: the front stops about a millimetre down, inside the decidua, with 34% of the drawn stroma to spare — the brake working. Narrating accreta over a picture with no muscle in it would teach a depth the student cannot see.
deferred_beats.where_it_belongs: its own scene. "Abnormal implantation" is a clinical topic with its own structures (tube, os, myometrium, caesarean scar) and it is not a view of the normal process. Until that exists the text belongs in the sequence mode, which is in deferred_modes. Filed as a gap rather than silently dropped, because this is the half of the topic that explains, as the paragraph itself says, half of third-trimester obstetrics.

gaps: ROUTED TO 3d_anatomy, not to its first preferred mode. CURRICULUM.json lists preferred_modes ["sequence","diagram"] for Implantation and the SVG-era scene took the first of them. This conversion moves it to 3d_anatomy on the queue item's instruction, and both original modes are retained in deferred_modes rather than discarded. The curriculum's declared views[] are ["mechanism","associated_organs"]; this scene carries eight mechanism views and two associated_organs views, so the contract is met.

THE ENDOMETRIUM IS DRAWN AS A WINDOW, NOT WHOLE. A secretory endometrium is 5-7 mm thick; what is built is a 2.6 mm wide patch of its superficial 2.0 mm, at TRUE SCALE with no scale break. The window grows with the conceptus (45 to 142 units of radius) so that a 180 um embryo and a 1 mm one are both legible — the geometry is true scale at every t and what changes is how much wall is in frame.

NO MYOMETRIUM IS DRAWN, and therefore accreta, increta and percreta are narrated in deferred_beats[] and not drawn. Placing a myometrial boundary at the bottom of the drawn window would put it at 2 mm instead of 5-7 mm, which is exactly the scale break the paragraph above refuses.

NO BODY SIDE IS DECLARED OR DRAWN. Every structure but the gland and the spiral artery is a surface of revolution about the y axis, so this model has no left/right landmark and a mirror of it would be indistinguishable. RENDER-STANDARD's "A DECLARED AXIS IS NOT A PROVED ONE, AND A SYMMETRIC MODEL CANNOT PROVE ITS OWN" is met by not making the claim: nothing this scene narrates names a side.

PINOPODES AND ADHESION MOLECULES ARE NOT DRAWN. A pinopode is about 1 um — a tenth of one unit — and integrin binding has no form at any scale this model works at. Views 1 and 3 narrate both and draw the epithelium they are properties of. This is why view 3 is the CUT view: adhesion's only drawable content is that the trophoblast is against the sheet and not yet through it.

THE BILAMINAR DISC IS DRAWN AS A FLATTENING LENS, NOT AS TWO LAYERS. Epiblast and hypoblast are not separate parts here. That boundary is the subject of embryology__weeks-1-2-implantation-bilaminar-disc__bilaminar-embryonic-disc, the next item in this topic, and duplicating it badly here would give a student two different pictures of one thing. What IS asserted is the flattening the narration names, measured, in claim B10-disc-flat.

THE LACUNAE ARE DRAWN AS SOLIDS INSIDE A TRANSLUCENT SHELL, not as holes cut through it. They are spaces in the syncytiotrophoblast and the honest alternative — perforating the shell with a real radial partition — was rejected as a fragile two-piece construction whose two laminae become coincident wherever the perforation closes. The containment is published by name in the model's PARTITION, the shell is drawn at 0.52 opacity in every beat that shows them, and RENDER-STANDARD 3.x is explicit that this is what a teaching figure does.

THE SVG VERSION'S PEEL_LAYER AND TRACE_STRUCTURE OPS ARE GONE. PEEL_LAYER (old beat 6) addressed a diagram-engine layer stack this scene does not have, and the cross-section does its work. TRACE_STRUCTURE (old beats 2 and 4) is DEGRADED to a highlight by the procedural adapter (viz3d.js capabilities), and both of its traces were over teaching beats rather than over parts — the sequence they traced is now three and three beats respectively, each drawing its own stage.

THE SYNCYTIOTROPHOBLAST'S POLE-TO-ABEMBRYONIC THICKNESS RATIO IS CONSTANT ACROSS THE WEEK (4.52, measured). The absolute thickness grows from 5.5 um to 72 um at the pole, but the shape of the asymmetry is a declared profile and not a function of t, so claim B5-asymmetry is true at every t and does not pin its beat. Said here so a reviewer does not read it as a pinning claim.

THE CLOCK IS LINEAR IN REAL TIME (day = 6 + 7t), unlike every neighbouring embryology model. That is deliberate and is argued in the model's header section 1: this scene's narration quotes a day in almost every sentence, so a beat's t and the day its words name are the same number twice.

ONE SOLVED RATE, ANCHORED ON ONE SENTENCE. SINK_RATE comes from "by day nine the embryo is under the surface" and nothing else. Everything else about the depth is a prediction of it against the growth law and is checked rather than set: the day the epithelium is breached, how wide the defect gets and when it is widest, the day it closes, the plug's window, the capsularis's thickness, and the depth on days 12 and 13. If the growth law moves, the rate moves with it.

LYS_FRAC = 0.62 IS A DECLARED INPUT, not a measured one. It says what share of the room the conceptus makes is digested rather than pushed aside, and it is the only number in the model chosen to make a prediction land in a published range (the 50-150 um elevation of acceptance row H). A reviewer should read it as a drawing decision with a stated consequence.

WHAT THE LATE BEATS DO NOT DRAW, AND WHY — the visibility walk's doing rather than an oversight. The camera is refitted per beat to what is visible, so a structure that spans the whole drawn window holds the subject under 1% of the frame. The decidua parietalis is the full 2.6 mm slab and is not drawn in beats 3, 5, 6, 8 and 10; the surface epithelium spans the same radius and is not drawn in beat 8; and the decidua basalis at day 13 is not stroma that hugs the conceptus but a slab reaching the floor of the drawn window, so it is not drawn in beat 10. The wall at full width is established in beats 1, 2, 4, 7 and 9, and beat 9 is where the healed-over epithelium is SEEN — beat 8 still asserts it in claim B8-healed, which reads the model, and no longer draws it. MEASURED, which is why each of those came out: with the slab drawn, the blood beat 8 highlights measured 0.454% of the frame by id-pick and 0.146% by the alpha-aware diff, under the 0.30% pointed-at floor, and the beat cleared only because the walk passes on either measure (review finding F1). It now measures 0.475% and 1.194%. Beat 10's villi went from 0.158% to 0.539%. RENDER-STANDARD 3.aa in its general form: what a beat draws decides what can be seen in it, so the shown list is part of the claim.

THE EMBRYONIC POLE MARKER IS NOT DRAWN IN BEAT 2. At day 6 it is 0.019% of the frame — the conceptus is 180 um in an 870 um frame and the marker is a pin on its surface — against the visibility walk's 0.30% floor. It is drawn in the cut beats, where it clears the floor. Beat 2 names the pole in its relationship label instead of drawing a marker nobody can see.

COMPARE_STRUCTURES IS NOT USED, THOUGH THE SVG VERSION USED IT TWICE. viz3d lists it as a native op for the procedural adapter, but its side-by-side layout displaces the compared structures while the per-view camera refit is computed from the undisplaced bounding box, so under framing_strict the subject is clipped at the frame border. Measured on beat 5: 2486 subject pixels on a border row with the op, 0 without it. The comparison it was making is carried by the section itself, which draws the two layers concentric and touching. A scene that genuinely needs two things moved apart should expect to fight the framing pass.

THE DECIDUA CAPSULARIS HAS FIVE KEYS, ALL PINNED. It does not exist before about day 7.4, so by the model header's section 3 it may not carry an unpinned ref: viz3d resolves an unpinned ref at t = 1 at mount and restages every structure that arrived on every SET_STAGE, so beats 1 to 4 would resolve it to reason:none and it would be gone for the rest of the session. The scene's first version did carry it unpinned, and check 6 of render-implantation.mjs found it at four t values — this scene walking into the fault it was written to avoid, caught by its own proof.

THE SPIRAL ARTERY IS ONE VESSEL AND THE LACUNAE ARE OPENED AT ONE PLACE. Review finding F1 is fixed by making the vessel breach the trophoblast and the blood continuous into the lacunae, and the site is SOLVED — the nearest pair between the uneroded centreline and the lacunar band on the grid the band is built on, so nothing about it is typed in. What is still a simplification is the COUNT: a real day-12 site has many spiral arteries opening all round the decidua basalis, and this one draws a single vessel in the section plane because that is the one a cut specimen shows. The beat narrates "maternal capillaries", plural; the picture shows one of them. Declared rather than quietly accepted.

THE SYNCYTIOTROPHOBLAST IS NOT PERFORATED AT THE BREACH. The vessel's mouth is drawn INSIDE the shell's own radial band and the shell is a complete surface of revolution, so the shell's outer surface runs through the breach rather than opening at it — the same construction, and the same reason, as the lacunae themselves (the gap above). It is why the first-hit test in acceptance row S excludes, by name read off the model's PARTITION, the surfaces the model publishes as containing the blood: including them would report the published idiom as a defect. A reviewer who thinks the perforation is worth the fragility should say so — it is a real alternative and it was rejected rather than missed.

THE VILLUS COVER IS A DECLARED FRACTION, NOT A MEASURED ONE. Finding F3 replaced a containment test that passed at a clearance of 0.016% with a solved length leaving 25% of the local syncytiotrophoblast thickness over each tip, and 0.25 is a drawing decision with a stated consequence in the same sense LYS_FRAC is: it is chosen so the cover is visible at the scale the beat is drawn at (18 um at the pole) while the column stays long enough to be a column (41 um solved, 48 um measured on the built mesh including the dome). No source was consulted for the ratio. A reviewer should attack the number before the geometry.

ONE TROPHOBLAST BEFORE CONTACT, AND NOTHING BETWEEN. Finding F4 added an undifferentiated layer for the window before adhesion, so beat 2 no longer draws a syncytiotrophoblast three beats before the beat that says it comes into existence. What is NOT drawn is the splitting itself: the layer is replaced by the two, over the adhesion window, rather than shown dividing. Acceptance row V asserts the window and the band; no beat sits inside the transition, so nothing is claimed about it.

EVERY FIGURE THIS FILE AND THE MODEL STATE ABOUT THEMSELVES NOW LIVES IN ACCEPTANCE.declared, and row T asserts it. Finding F5: the comment beside SINK_RATE said 141.88 where the solve returns 151.535 — the model's one solved number, described 6.4% wrong by the only thing that described it. That is RENDER-STANDARD's cardiac-looping axis comment arriving again, and this model's own section 6: a note in a file is a claim, including your own.

THE SPIRAL ARTERY IS DRAWN TRANSLUCENT IN THE CUT BEATS, at 0.45, and that is the second half of finding F1's framing. The vessel is a swept tube, and the +cut flag reaches the surfaces of revolution rather than the tubes (the gland says the same of itself), so it is built WHOLE and stands proud of the cut face. With an opaque wall the lumen was hidden along the vessel's whole course and the only maternal blood a student could see was the lacunar pool — on a beat whose sentence is "their blood spills into the lacunae". Same idiom and same argument as the 0.52 on the syncytiotrophoblast. The honest alternative, sectioning the tube, needs a cut that reaches VizKit's swept shells and is a kit change, not a scene one.
